text: Scheidt's patent can stack its step: shift, mixed alphabet, shift, mixed alphabet, shift. Three short secret words would give the three shifts; Sanborn spoke of 'triple matrixes'.
Each known letter ties one letter of each word; any two decide the third. A compiled search with that rule decides every choice of the two mixed alphabets and every length triple up to 10 exactly.
Where the known letters give 4 or more checks, nothing fits K4 or a scrambled copy. With fewer checks K4 fits as often as the copies. F3.4 closed; the few-check cells are too weak to decide.
